programs.title: Shells: Shaped by Nature
programs.desc: Viewers will learn the secrets of African shells.They will discover the history of the evolution of the delightful forms that nature has given them.

programs.title: Killer Whale Chronicles
programs.desc: Since killer whales began attacking boats near Gibraltar, there has been some question as to whether their behavior is a threat or just playful.In a two-part documentary narrated by singer and orca enthusiast Sarah Connor, we learn about the advanced hunting techniques of these cetaceans, as well as their developed social intelligence and precise cooperation.We will see how older orcas teach younger ones to control their bodies.We will also delve into their world of emotions, observing how they mourn the loss of loved ones and how they have fun.

programs.title: Wildes Südafrika - Der 8. Kontinent
programs.desc: South Africa, like the entire continent, is very diverse.This is a place where cold-loving penguins live alongside ostriches that live in sandy areas.Sea snails and lively chameleons also thrive in this climate.South Africa has distinctive geographical features as well as extreme climatic conditions.Wild animals are exposed to constant changes in living conditions.On the west coast you can meet predatory sea lions that specialize in hunting young Cape boobies;in the south, giant crocodiles, lions and deer, and inland - elephants.

programs.title: Underdogs
programs.desc: Ryan Reynold takes a closer look at inconspicuous creatures with unusual skills.Watching their mating rituals and parenting strategies, it becomes clear that they are the heroes of the animal kingdom.

programs.title: Alaska's Grizzly Gauntlet
programs.desc: Prince William Sound is home to black bears.Three thousand individuals live there, and over 100,000 in the entire territory of Alaska.Survivalist Les Stroud will take a closer look at them, and what's more, he will come face to face with them.However, before he decides to meet, he must learn more about the habits of the subjects of his research.He will be helped by someone who knows everything about the local flora and fauna.Stroud's guide spent decades observing black bears.Thanks to it, the traveler will learn what dangers he may encounter after crossing the borders of the kingdom of these predators.The expedition begins when they are preparing for the arrival of winter.They need to increase their weight because the additional protective layer is useful in hostile weather conditions.Bears are looking for food, but if they choose the wrong place, they are in serious danger.First of all, they must be vigilant - every rustle means that an unwanted companion has appeared.Viewers will see how predators deal with them.It is also worth mentioning that these animals want to be left in peace wherever they are.This is why Stroud does not enter their lairs, because a confrontation may prove painful.

programs.desc: Nat Geo Wild explores the beauty and ferocity of the animal kingdom, offering an intimate look at the world’s most incredible creatures in their habitats.

programs.title: Built to Survive
programs.desc:
Phil Breslin, a filmmaker and knowledge popularizer from Australia, begins his expedition through the most difficult corners of this continent.During the journey, he talks about animals that managed to master the art of survival.Each episode introduces three species and discusses their unique characteristics.From harsh deserts to seas to forests to rivers, Phil introduces viewers to a variety of ecosystems, showing which animals are best adapted to challenging environmental conditions
Phil Breslin, born in Australia, has been talking with passion and enthusiasm for years about the nature of Kangaroo Land, which stands out from all other continents.It is inhabited by animal species that cannot be found in other parts of the world.There are extreme conditions in the antipodes, which forced the inhabitants to develop unique adaptation strategies.Divided into several parts, the document presents masters of survival in various habitats - in rainforests, deserts, swamps, as well as on the coast and in the ocean.Antipodes teeming with life. The naturalist begins his expedition in the hot and humid Australian rainforest.Among the lush tree crowns, you have the chance to spot a tree hawk with its young, as well as the largest snake in Australia - an amethyst python.He observes with delight the colorful cassowary - one of the most dangerous birds in the world.During his further escapade, he encounters more animals that arouse respect.While crossing the swamps, he has a chance to take a closer look at the massive saltwater crocodile, which is one of the most dangerous predators.The rocky coastlines are the kingdom of the white-bellied piscifer - a bird from the Accipitridae family, which boasts impressive talons.
